Description: From the edition published by Chatterjee in Calcutta at the end of the 19th century. Script: Bengali. Notes: Transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Mark S.G. Dyczkowski. Revision 0: 28/01/2007.
Publication year: Pre-1900.
Place of publication: Calcutta Country of publication: India Title: Kaṅkālamālinītantra
Oṃ, salutations to the venerable Guru. Śrī Bhairavī said:
O Lord of Tripura, Great Īśāna, beloved of Pārvatī’s life-breath!
O Śūlapāṇi, revered by the world, tell me the cause of the social classes (varṇas).
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O lady of excellent hips, I shall describe the supreme distinction of the letters;
it must not be disclosed, O Great Goddess, but because of my affection for you, O eloquent one, I shall speak.
O My beloved, who are proud of your great youth! Listen to that essential nature by knowing which yogis attain the state beyond the qualities (nirguṇatva). 3.
That Lord of the World, whose nature is the Brahman of Sound, consists of the letters from 'A' to 'Kṣa';
[his forms are] Vidyujjihvā, Karālāsyā, Garjinī, and Dhūmrabhairavī.
Kālarātri, Vidārī, Mahāraudrī, Bhayaṃkarī, Saṃhāriṇī, Karālinī, Ūrdhvakeśī, and Ugrabhairavī. (5)
Bhīmākṣī, Ḍākinī, Rudraḍākinī, and Caṇḍikā—these are to be known as the vowels (svaras) among the letters, O Kaulinī; now hear [the description] of the consonants (vyañjanas).
Krodhīśa, Vāmana, Caṇḍa, Vikārin, Unmattabhairava, Jvālāmukha, Raktadaṃṣṭra, Hasitāṅga, and Vaḍavāmukha. || 7 ||
Vidyunmukha, Mahājvāla, Kapālī, Bhīṣaṇa, Ruru, Saṃhārī, Bhairava, Daṇḍī, Valibhuj, and Ugraśūladhṛk.
Siṃhanādin, Kapardin, Karālāgni, Bhayaṅkara, Bahurūpin, Mahākāla, Jīvātman, and Kṣatajokṣita. || 9 ||
The shatterer of armies, the one of blood, the Lord of Caṇḍī, he whose banner is fire;
he whose banner is the bull, whose mouth is the sky, and whose nature is the devouring of the three worlds. || 10 ||
These consonants (vyañjana) are to be known as those beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'kṣa' in their respective order;
however, the vowels (varṇa), from 'a' to 'kṣa', are Śiva and Śakti.
These fifty phonemes are the eternal forms of Brahman;
without knowledge of them, there can be no accomplishment in the Vāmamārga, O Guru.
O auspicious daughter of the mountain, those oceans of phonemes (varṇasāgara), consisting of the three qualities (guṇatraya), have been declared;
O daughter of the mountain, having made Vidyujjihvā the beginning and Caṇḍikā the end.
The castes consist of the quality of *sattva*; now hear those consisting of the quality of *rajas*:
from Krodhīśa to Daṇḍin, the consonants are traditionally held to be *rājasa*.
Beginning from the color of the fire-eater (smoke) up to the devouring of the three worlds, they should be known as being of the nature of darkness; hear now, O beloved, those born from them. 15.
The syllable *gu* signifies darkness, and the syllable *ru* signifies that which brings about its cessation;
because it causes the cessation of darkness, it is called *guru*. (16)
The letter *ga* is declared to be the bestower of perfection; the letter *ra* is the remover of sin;
and the letter *u* shall be Viṣṇu—the Guru himself, whose nature consists of the triad. (17)
In the beginning, this eternal Śabdabrahman is born;
it is adorned by Vasujihvā, Kālarātri, and Rudraḍākinī.
O Dear One, the seed-syllable of poison is the beginning of the Veda, which is certainly Hālāhala;
and Oṃ is Caṇḍīśa, mounted upon blood and adorned by Dhūmrabhairavī. (19)
The seed-syllable of Lakṣmī is proclaimed as being joined with *nāda* and *bindu*:
*Śrīṃ*. *Krodhīśa*, mounted upon blood and adorned by *Dhūmrabhairavī*. (20)
O Goddess, the seed-syllable of the name is proclaimed to be joined with the *nāda* and *bindu*. [The mantra is:
*Dhrīṃ*, [formed] with *Krodhīśa* (*va*), *Ula* (*la*), *Bhṛt* (*bha*), [and] *Valibhuj* (*ra*), along with *dhūmra-bhairavī*, *nāda*, and *bindu*. (21)
The triple-formed Manmatha, the seed-syllable of desire that deludes the three worlds—*krīṃ*. Seated upon blood, with a face like the sky, he is adorned by the smoky Bhairavī. || 22 ||
It is known as Māyā and Lajjā, enriched with the beautiful splendor of Nāda and Bindu:
KRĪṂ. It has the Sky as its mouth, resides in Vidārī, and is adorned by Nāda and Bindu. (23)
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, know that *hūṃ* is the seed-syllable of Wrath (*krodhabīja*) at the time of the *kūrca*.
It has the sky as its mouth, is enriched by the Night of Time (*kālarātri*), and is joined with the armor-syllable and the bindu. (24)

The spoken word is the seed-syllable (bīja), O stainless one who delights in the family tradition (kulācāra). It has the sky as its mouth, is mounted upon blood (kṣataja), and belongs to the Ḍākinī through the nasal sound (nāda) and the bindu. 25.
The Jyotirmantra has been fully declared; it destroys even the most heinous sins.
Having taken up the fierce Bhairavī, who is joined with the Nāda and Bindu, [utter] "Drāḥ. (26)
O Dear One, know that the elemental seed-syllable of speech is that of Sarasvatī;
O Śivā, "Aiṃ" is known as the mantra of the weapon, the great net of the fire of dissolution.
This goad (aṅkuśa) is named Raktakrodhīśa Bhīma, endowed with Nāda and Bindu:
*krauḥ*. Dviṭha is Śiva; Vahni-jāyā is Svāhā, the beloved of the Fire-god. (28)
The offering of blood for Dhūmrabhairavī is joined with *svāhā* and *svāhā*;
the supreme seed-syllable of Kiṅkiṇī is conjoined with the *nāda* and the *bindu*. (29)

Dṛī! This great mantra known as Viśikhā consists of the syllable joined with *nāda* and *bindu*, situated in red, and accompanied by the devourer of offerings (*balibhojana*) seated upon a gaping mouth. (30)
Having split [the letter] *dū*, one should look at the one in the secret place (*guhya*) smeared with blood;
joined with the *nāda* and the *bindu*, it is to be known as *piśitāśana*. || 31 ||
The seed-syllable that brings about the end of the age, blazing with smoke and fierce fire, with upward-pointing hair and lunar drops, was revealed by the wives of the heroes.
Situated above Saṃhāriṇī is Ka, and the one with matted hair (R);
the seed-syllable joined with Nāda and Bindu is known as Vaitālika. || 33 ||

The seed-syllable of Krodhīśa, together with the nasal bindu, situated at the secret place (guhya) as Saṃhāriṇī, is called the "trembling" (kampinī) seed; it is known as Caṇḍikā and is captivating to the mind. 34.
Taking up Kapardin, who stands drenched in blood and joined with Dhūmrabhairavī, this is Dhvāṅkṣa, possessed of the Nāda and Bindu. (35)
Prīṃ. Taking two plantains, it is adorned by Mahākāla;
with the sound "Namaḥ," it is called the cloud named Caṇḍikā. (36)
Ṭha Ṭha! O Dear One, Phetkāriṇī is said to be the smoke-bannered fire situated in the fire of dissolution, possessing the bindu of the Lord of Secrets, and joined with Dhūmrabhairavī. 37.
*Sphīṃ*. This is situated in blood, has the sky as its mouth, and is adorned with a dot (*bindu*), a crescent moon, and the *khadyota*;
it is renowned as the "Firefly" (*khadyota*) and is joined with Grasini and Kālarātri. 38.

O Goddess, this seed-syllable, whose essence is Vaivasvata, is mounted upon the letter *drū* drenched in blood, endowed with the nasal sound (*nāda*) and the bindu, and adorned with the *vidārī* vowel. (39)
Thus ends the first chapter in the *Kaṅkālamālinītantra*, within the *Sārghalakṣa* text of the Dakṣiṇāmnāya. || 1 ||
Now begins the second chapter.
The venerable Pārvatī said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Nīlakaṇṭha, whose wealth is asceticism!
O Mahādeva, [tell me of] the Yonimudrā and the three principles (tattvas), which are higher than the highest.
O Mahādeva, wielder of the Pināka bow, let this very thing be explained to me.
The illustrious Lord said:
Listen, O Goddess of gods; I am your servant, O lady of virtuous vows. I shall speak of the three principles, which are most secret and highly meritorious, O fair-faced one.
The essence of essences, the supreme secret, most hidden and well-ascertained—O Goddess, since even doubt arises [regarding it], how can I possibly speak of it? (3)
I shall speak, O Great Goddess, O beautiful lady, by your command;
for if that is not told, O Goddess, your anger will arise.
O Goddess, O beloved, if you become angry, my ruin will follow;
for the sake of the mantra, O dear one, the consciousness of the mantra bestows virtue, wealth, and desire.
O Maheśānī, the Yonimudrā is the third, having the form of Brahman;
for one who recites the mantra without knowing it, no accomplishment arises.
Having understood this, one should begin and perform it; for by not performing it, one perishes.
O Maheśānī, the Yonimudrā is the direct means for accomplishing liberation.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, my beloved, just as you are dear to me, so too is your womb always dear to me, O Supreme Goddess; I am a servant to you by means of your womb. (8)
O fair-faced one, O Goddess of gods, O lotus-faced one, by the grace of your womb, having conquered death, I shall be eternally known as Mṛtyuñjaya (the Conqueror of Death).
O Great Goddess, within your womb the universe, with all that is moving and unmoving, constantly resides; O Goddess, [therein] dwell Brahmā and the other inhabitants of the three heavens.
O Maheśānī, having placed the wonderful tail-feathers of a peacock [there],
O Maheśānī of pure smiles, Kṛṣṇa beheld it in the form of a vulva.
O lady of excellent limbs, by holding [this] upon one's head, one may bring the three worlds under control;
O Great Goddess, I meditate upon your vulva day and night.
O lovely one, having seen the cosmic egg right there, I see nothing else;
it is your supreme city of the womb, from which camphor-like thrills arise.
O Great Goddess, your womb is well-worshipped by the three principles;
joined with semen and menstrual blood, it is the manifest temple of the God of Love.
I do not know what deed was performed, O Kālikā, lotus-eyed one, in your womb, O Great Goddess, for this reason, O fair-faced one. (15)
O Supreme Goddess, I constantly [meditate upon] the Yoni-mudrā and the seed-syllable of the Yoni;
O Goddess, by the grace of the Yoni-mudrā, I am the conqueror of death. (16)
O Great Goddess, O Beloved, listen as I declare the seed-syllables of the sources:
first, O Supreme Goddess, is the Yoginī Rudrayoginī. (17)
Having extracted it with great effort, make it endowed with the seed-syllable of power (Bala-bīja);
joined with the Vindu and the half-moon, this is the seed-syllable that fascinates the three worlds.
O Dear One, having indeed bound the Yonimudrā according to the previously mentioned sequence,
O Maheśānī, one should recite the Yonibīja one hundred and eight times.
O beloved, who indeed would be capable of describing the greatness of him who obtains the fruit by reciting [this] one hundred and eight times, O Goddess of Devas? (20)
He who, with a serene soul, worships the one in the form of the Yoni in secret, he indeed worships the entire universe; Brahmā and the other dwellers of the three heavens do not equal him.
O Great Goddess, your womb is the nature of the Supreme Brahman; O Great Goddess, beloved one, your womb is the enchantress of Bhava.
O Great Goddess, one should encircle your vulva with the thread of accomplishment (siddhisūtra). O Great Goddess, O fair-faced one, the thread of accomplishment is of three kinds. (23)
Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and likewise Suṣumnā—this triad [leads] to the womb consisting of eternal bliss, which sports in manifold pleasures. (24)
"O Goddess Pārvatī, during the time of passion, I do not reach the end;
O Maheśānī, my liṅga pierces through the entire universe. (25)
Nevertheless, O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, I do not reach the end;
O Great Sovereign, I do not know what kind of passage your womb possesses. (26)
O Great Goddess, your womb is the primordial form of Prakṛti;
it is the eternal Kuṇḍalinī, the supreme Great Kuṇḍalinī.
O Supreme Goddess, O fair-faced one, he who always, having beheld the Yoni, recites the seed-syllable known as Bhaga—which is the very form of the Bhaga—O lady of excellent hips; || 28 ||
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, by binding the *yoni-mudrā* with the seed-syllable of the *bhaga* and reciting it one hundred and eight times, O beloved, one shall become equal to me. (29)
O Great Goddess, one should diligently practice union within your womb;
by that mere act of union, he becomes identical with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, and he shall become wealthy, eloquent, and attain equality with the Lord of Speech (Bṛhaspati). || 30 ||
The Goddess said: O Nīlakaṇṭha, O Mahādeva, please tell me the secret out of compassion;
if it is not told to me, O Lord, then I shall cast off this body.
The illustrious Lord said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, O you with limbs as dark as Kṛṣṇa, O you with eyes like a wagtail bird, O you of beautiful eyes!
This secret must indeed be kept hidden; it bestows the fruit of all desires.
It is held that there are thirty-five million channels (nāḍikās) in the body;
among them, ten are said to be principal, and among those, three are established as the most essential.
O Goddess of the Gods, I am a yogi who, having immersed the principal spinal column at its tip— which consists of the forms of the moon, sun, and fire— into the suṣumnā.
O Supreme Goddess, one should meditate upon her in the form of a vulva within the six cakras; first, O Supreme Goddess, is the ādhāra with four petals.

That place, exceedingly difficult to attain, possesses the luster of molten gold and the brilliance of ten million flashes of lightning, and is surrounded by the four castes of celestial singers (Gandharvas).
O Goddess of gods, within that pericarp is a most beautiful triangle,
which consists of will, knowledge, and action, and whose nature is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

In the center, one should likewise contemplate the self-manifested liṅga (svayambhūliṅga), which is eternally encircled by Kuṇḍalinī; O Queen of the Gods, one should meditate upon it as the letter 'La', known as the triangle (trikoṇa). || 38 ||

Having meditated upon the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) therein, one should meditate upon Kāmadeva; having likewise meditated upon the seed-syllable within that very womb, there is indeed the taking up [of the embryo]. (39)
O Goddess of gods, O Great Mistress, O Beloved of Prāṇa, one should contemplate movement in the feet, emission in the anus, and smelling in the nose, O passionate one. (40)
Then one should meditate upon the Ḍākinī and the supreme, worshipful Śakti;
O Mother Girijā, O Gaṇeśvarī, having brought these down to the earth.
In the midst of that, O beloved, is indeed the form of the Liṅga encircled by Kuṇḍalinī;
there [resides] the eternal Kuṇḍalinī, whose nature is supreme bliss.
There, O fair-faced one, one who desires accomplishment should perform meditation upon her who has the radiance of ten million moons and whose nature is that of the Supreme Brahman. (43)
She has four arms and three eyes, and likewise displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness; she holds a book and a lute, and is borne upon a lion.
O Maheśvarī, having brought that previously mentioned auspicious earth, which possesses various forms and is formidable, into the fragrance, they go to their own seat.
Having drawn up the individual soul (jīvātman) by means of the syllable *praṇava* alone, O Daughter of the Mountain King,
the practitioner, together with Kuṇḍalinī, takes up the fragrance of love.
O Goddess, with the mantra "So 'ham," one should cause [the breath] to enter the Svādhiṣṭhāna;
that lotus, located at the base of the liṅga, is six-petalled and has the luster of vermilion.
It is beautifully adorned with the faces of the disputants, which resemble throbbing valor;
one should meditate upon Varuṇa in its pericarp, and thereupon Hari as well. (48)
O fair-faced one, having visualized the youthful Rākiṇī as the Śakti,
[one should contemplate] the water upon the sacrificial post of the organ of taste, which is eager with desire.
Having brought these, as well as the fragrance and the nectar, to the delightful Śivā,
one should lead the individual soul, Kuṇḍalinī, and the nectar to the Maṇipūraka.
O beloved, having led that lotus with its petals pointing in the directions by means of the supreme yoga,
it is blue in color, like a flash of lightning, and adorned with the consonants from *ḍa* to *pha*.
O lady of beautiful hips, having meditated upon the Fire within its pericarp, the practitioner [should know that] Rudra himself is the agent there of the dissolution of all things. (52)
Endowed with the power (śakti) of Lākinī, one should meditate upon him in that charming [place];
having made the faculty of sight there consist of light, one should worship it. 53.
O fortunate one, O highly blessed one, having taken this essence and form, one should lead the individual soul, in the form of Kuṇḍalinī, to the Anāhata [cakra]. || 54 ||
That lotus, resembling the bandhūka flower, has twelve spokes;
it is adorned with the beloved of Hara, who is beautified by the radiant letters from *ka* to *ṭha*.
In its pericarp, one should meditate upon Vāyu, who dwells in the abode of the individual soul (jīva),
and there, the circle of the womb (yoni-maṇḍala), resplendent with a Bāṇaliṅga.
There, the sense organ of touch belonging to air is conjoined with the power (śakti) of Kākinī;
having joined this form [with her], O lover of Ramanaka in heaven! (57)
Then, one should place the life-force Kuṇḍalinī as the tactile sensation in the Viśuddha [cakra],
which is the smoke-colored throat-lotus adorned with the sixteen vowels.
In its pericarp is space (ākāśa) together with Śiva and Kāriṇī;
having established speech and hearing within that space, O daughter of the Mountain. (59)
O Śāṅkarī, my beloved, having brought these [vowels] into touch and sound,
one should cause Kuṇḍalinī to digest them and place the sound upon the leaf of the Ājñā-cakra.
The lotus of the eye is white in color and has two petals adorned with the sense-organ;
in its pericarp is a triangle where the Bāṇaliṅga is situated.
And here, the mind always shines, marked by the power of Hākinī, characterized by intellect, primordial nature, and ego, and supreme in its splendor. (62)
O Maheśvarī, one should also fix the individual soul, the Kuṇḍalinī,
and the mind within the great lotus of the thousand petals.
The eternal lotus has a thousand petals, is white in color, and faces downward;
it is resplendent with the shimmering letters beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa'.
O Goddess of gods, within its pericarp are the inner self (antarātman) and then the Guru, as well as the orb of the sun and the orb of the moon. (65)
From that, the wind of great sound is known to proceed from the *brahmarandhra*;
in that aperture resides the emission (*visarga*), which is eternal bliss and stainless.
Above that is the goddess Śaṅkhinī, who effects creation, maintenance, and destruction;
and below her, O Queen of the Gods, is that which resides in the center of the four mandalas.
Having visualized a triangle there, one should meditate upon Kailāsa;
O Great Goddess, having established a steady mind in this place. (68)
The living soul has transcended disease and is no longer subject to rebirth;
herein resides the eternally risen digit of the new moon (amākalā), devoid of increase or decrease.
In the midst of that is the seventeenth digit, called Nirvāṇa, which is crooked;
it is of the nature of fire, called Nirodhikā, and is contained within that which is termed Nirvāṇa.
Above that unmanifest Nāda is the supreme power of Nirvāṇa, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns, which is the source-form of all things.
Within this power, Śiva is to be known as changeless and stainless;
right here, O Goddess of the gods, is the Kuṇḍalī power in the form of a mudrā.
Moving again in that same manner into the supporting lotus—O Supreme Goddess, this has been described by me to you as the Yoni-mudrā. (73)
O Maheśvarī, without that perfected Supreme Self, one cannot carry away [the offering] by means of streams of divine nectar possessing the luster of lac. 74.
By means of this yoga, the practitioner-yogi should satisfy the deity;
through this, the perfection of the power of Kuṇḍalinī shall be attained, even by hundreds of millions of syllables.
Therefore, O Girijā, you too must guard this with great effort;
having meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī in the form of mantra within the circle of the six cakras.
Singing very sweetly from the center of the lotus, perpetually rising,
she goes through the aperture of Brahmā and enters her own abode.
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, having established that goddess in the *mūlādhāra*, perform the recitation of the garland strung with *citriṇī* beads, O beautiful one of the universe. (78)
The supreme, divine secret has been declared as the consciousness of mantra, as well as the knowledge of the consciousness of mudrās and the knowledge of the phonemes (varṇas). || 79 ||
O Goddess, O sweet-spoken one, this meaning of the mantra has been told to you out of affection;
O auspicious one, O fair-eyed one, without the knowledge of this, there can be no accomplishment.
Thus, O Goddess, this supreme play of the Yoni has been described to you.
The illustrious Lord said: O you who are worshipped by the world of gods and asuras, O servant of the womb of Pārvatī,
I now desire to hear the supreme armor (kavaca) of the womb.
The illustrious Lord said:
O beloved, by wearing and reciting which all powers become granters of boons—
of this armor (kavaca), the seer (ṛṣi) is Śrī Sadāśiva.
The meter is Gāyatrī, the deity is the eternal Yonirūpā;
O Goddess of the gods, her application (viniyoga) among the four aims of life is proclaimed. || 83 ||
Oṃ mam mām mim mīm mum mūm mem maim mom maum maṃ maḥ | (The right foot: May they protect my head, svāhā!
Oṃ mam mām mim mīm mum mūm mem maim mom maum maṃ maḥ.
Oṃ māṃ oṃ ākuṭāṃ, may they protect me, svāhā! Mam māṃ!
Oṃ maṃ māṃ miṃ mīṃ muṃ mūṃ meṃ maiṃ moṃ mauṃ maṃmaḥ, may they protect my heart and the right arm.
Oṃ maṃ māṃ miṃ mīṃ muṃ mūṃ meṃ maiṃ moṃ mauṃ maḥ.

Oṃ mam mām mim mīm mum mūm mem maim mom maum maṃ maḥ. May these protect my heart and the rest, up to my left arm. Oṃ mam mām mim mīm mum mūm mem maim mom maum maṃ maḥ. May these protect my right foot and my left foot at all times. Svāhā svāhā svāhā.
Oṃ mam mām mim mīm mum mūm mem maim mom maum maṃ maḥ.

May [the syllables] *ma*, *māṃ*, *mi*, *mīṃ*, *mu*, *mūṃ*, *meṃ*, *maiṃ*, *moṃ*, *mauṃ*, *maṃ*, *maḥ* protect my heart and other limbs, as well as my nose; *svāhā*. Oṃ! May *ma*, *māṃ*, *mi*, *mīṃ*, *mu*, *mūṃ*, *meṃ*, *maiṃ*, *moṃ*, *mauṃ*, *maṃ*, *maḥ* always protect my generative organ; *svāhā*. Oṃ! *ma*, *māṃ*, *mi*, *mīṃ*, *mu*, *mūṃ*, *meṃ*, *maiṃ*, *moṃ*, *mauṃ*, *maṃ*, *maḥ*.
For this is the womb-armor, a most wonderful secret;
whoever recites the mantra without knowing this shall find everything to be fruitless. (84)
Listen attentively to this supreme and divine secret:
O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one, one should recite the mantra over the yantra at the mūlādhāra.
O Maheśānī, O Varārohā, within the inner self at the Mūlādhāra, one should recite the eternal Yoni at each successive Cakra, O Maheśānī. (86)
O beloved, during an eclipse of the moon or sun, one should recite the armor-mantra (kavaca);
one may then enjoy one's own wife by means of the yantra, or even another woman.
Indeed, by the grace of this armor, the *yonimudrā* is perfected.
O lotus-faced goddess, having recited this armor, [one attains success]. 88.
This great narrative concerning sexual union was performed by me together with you;
by the grace of this armor, people attain the supreme goal. (89)
Having written it upon birch bark with *svayambhū* flowers,
or even with white flowers, yellow pigment (*rocanā*), and lac (*laktaka*).
Having fashioned a pill from gold, the person who possesses the Yantra shall be Śrī Sadāśiva himself, both in this world and in the next. 91.
One desiring accomplishment should recite this one hundred and eight times; what need is there for much speaking here? There is nothing superior to this:
"Homage to the Yoni, homage to the Yoni, homage again and again to Kuṇḍalinī. (92)

Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Explanation of the Yoni-mudrā and Other [Mudrās]," in the Kaṅkālamālinī-tantra, a work of one hundred and fifty thousand verses belonging to the Dakṣiṇāmnāya.
Now begins the third chapter.
The venerable Goddess said: "Now I desire to hear about the supreme worship of the Guru."
The illustrious Lord said: O Great Goddess, O fair-faced one, I shall tell you that which is not to be revealed:
the two syllables "Gu-ru" are the supreme Brahman, devoid of qualities. (1)
O Maheśānī, this great mantra is most secret and supreme among the supreme;
I shall now describe the meditation upon it—listen with reverence, O Pārvatī. (2)
One should meditate upon the radiant inner self seated upon a thousand-petaled lotus;
above that, in the center of the *nāda* and *bindu*, [he sits] upon a radiant lion-throne.
One should constantly meditate upon one's own guru, who resembles a mountain of silver,
seated in the vīrāsana posture and adorned with mudrās and ornaments.
Wearing bright garlands and garments, with hands granting boons and fearlessness, accompanied by Śakti on his left thigh, and gazing with compassion. || 5 ||
His beautiful body was embraced by his beloved with her left hand,
while she held a blue lotus in her right hand and was adorned with red ornaments.
Endowed with knowledge and bliss, the wise one should chant its name preceded by [the syllable] *Om*, and having worshipped it with mental offerings, he should perform the ritual arrangement.
Then one should offer fragrance, which has the earth as its essence, followed by mental flowers;
O Goddess, one should likewise offer incense, which has air as its essence, and a lamp with light.
One should offer nectar as the food offering (naivedya) and water whose essence is Varuṇa;
one should also give garments, a crown, and cloth, O my beloved.
Having worshipped the fly-whisk, the sandals, the parasol, and likewise the ornaments and decorations according to their respective mudrās and ritual procedures, one should then worship the Guru.
Having performed the recitation according to one's ability and having offered it, one should recite the armor-verse (*kavaca*).
Thus has the excellent worship of the Guru been fully explained to you. (11)
The Goddess said:
O Great God, Lord of Beings, tell me that armor (kavaca) for him.
The illustrious Lord said: Now, O Sovereign Goddess, I shall tell you the armor (kavaca) which bestows liberation;
without the knowledge of which, O Goddess, there is neither spiritual perfection nor the attainment of the true goal.
O Girijā, even Brahmā and the others are remembered as victorious everywhere through his grace; by him, all the Vedas and Āgamas are preceded [and brought forth]. (14)
O Goddess of the gods, for this armor-mantra (kavaca), Viṣṇu is declared to be the seer (ṛṣi); the meter (chandas) is Virāṭ, and the deity is the Guru-god Śiva himself. (15)
The application is proclaimed within the path of knowledge regarding the fourfold aims;
the Guru is white as camphor in the great thousand-petaled lotus. 16.
May he whose power resides in his left thigh protect me from all sides;
may the Guru known as Parama protect my head, O beloved.
May he known as Parāpara protect my nose; may Parameṣṭhin protect my mouth;
and may Prahlādānandanātha always protect my throat. (18)
May Sanakānanda, the leader of the Kumārānandas, and Vaśiṣṭhanandanātha protect my two arms and my heart at all times. 17.
May the bliss of wrath protect my hips; may the bliss of pleasure protect my feet;
may the bliss of meditation protect all my limbs; and may the bliss of awakening protect me in the forest.
"May all gurus everywhere protect you, for all are the very form of the Lord.
Thus, O auspicious one, O Śivā, this supreme armor has been told to you.
To one devoid of devotion and of evil conduct, he would grant death;
yet, O Goddess, O Beloved, by merely reciting, retaining, or hearing this very [text], [one attains the opposite]. 22.
Mantras become perfected; what else shall I tell you?
[This occurs] on the neck, on the right arm, or on the crest-lock, O Goddess worshipped by heroes. (23)
By wearing it, one destroys sin just as the Gaṅgā destroys impurity;
O Dear One, if one should recite the mantra without knowing this armor (kavaca), [it is ineffective].
Having rendered all that fruitless, the Guru certainly departs;
when Śiva is angry, the Guru is the protector, but when the Guru is angry, there is no one at all.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Lord of the worlds, O God, O Master, let the Gurugītā be told to me.
Śrī Śiva said:
Listen, O Tāriṇī; I shall proclaim the supreme Gītā consisting of Brahman.
I myself am the teacher of all scriptures and their illuminator. (27)
You alone, in the form of the Guru, are the sustainer of the lives of all people;
you are Gayā, the Gaṅgā, and Kāśī—you indeed are the entire universe.
Kāverī, Yamunā, Revā, Karatoyā, Sarasvatī,
Candrabhāgā, and Gautamī— you alone are the protectress of these lineages.
O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, I am not able to describe to you the entire cosmic egg, nor even ten million cosmic eggs, nor the entire web of ritual actions.
Having spoken thus again and again, and having meditated upon it, O Daughter of the Mountain, this man is but a mendicant;
how can you, being my mother, become the wife of embodied beings? (31)
"O Great Goddess, your discus transcends even the Supreme Self.
Thus has this Gītā of the Guru-deity Brahmā been told to you.
In brief, O Great Goddess, the Lord himself is the Guru;
this entire world is to be supported by him alone, for it rests solely upon the Guru.
O Goddess of the Gods, by pleasing him with three prostrations and the offering of various kinds of substances, the best of practitioners shall attain perfection.

Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Hymn of Armor and the Song of the Guru," in the *Śrī Kaṅkālamālinī Tantra*, a work of one hundred and fifty thousand verses belonging to the *Śrī Dakṣiṇāmnāya*.
Now begins the fourth chapter.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Lord Virūpākṣa, tell me the mantra of Mahākālī.
The illustrious Lord said:
Now, therefore, O beloved, I shall fully declare the mantra of Mahākālī, by the mere knowledge of which one becomes a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis). || 2 ||
In splendor he was equal to Viṣṇu, in luster like the sun, in purity equal to the pure, and in strength comparable to the wind. || 3 ||
He was equal to Vāgīśvara in speech, to the Lord of Wealth himself in riches,
equal to Śambhu in omniscience, and equal to Dādhīci in generosity.
By his command he was a king of gods, by his Brahmanical nature he was a lord of creatures, like Bhṛgu he was an ascetic, and like the moon he increased the joy of others. || 5 ||
In brilliance he was equal to fire; through devotion to Śiva and Kṛṣṇa, he was like Nārada; in form he was like Madana himself; and in majesty he resembled the sun.
In discussions of the scriptures, he was like Aṅgiras among the sons of Jamadagni by his resolve;
he was Bhairava himself among the Siddhas, destroying impurities just as the Gaṅgā does.
Or rather, O fair-faced one, what is the use of saying much? There is no obstacle whatsoever for him who remembers Mahākālī with his mind. (8)

One attains liberation through enjoyment by hearing from the mouth of the Guru this supreme Svāhā, which consists of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahma) and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation alone. || 9 ||
Listen to that vidyā which I shall declare, by which one attains the state of Bhairava:
Krodhīśa mounted upon blood, marked by Dhūmrabhairavī. (10)
A mantra endowed with both *nāda* and *bindu* is difficult to find even in heaven;
O beloved, there is no knowledge (*vidyā*) equal to this single-syllable mantra in the three worlds. (11)
Mahākālī is the secret vidyā who bestows accomplishment in the Kali age.
Now I shall further explain the supreme Dakṣiṇā Kālikā. 12.
Having uttered the Vāgbhava seed-syllable, and after that the Kāmarāja,
and then the Māyā seed-syllable— O auspicious one, this is declared to be the three-syllabled mantra.
Then Kāmarāja, then Kūrca, and after that Māyābīja; another three-syllabled mantra has been proclaimed, O Dear One, which bestows the fruits previously mentioned. (14)
Having uttered "Hālāhala," followed by the two "Māyās" (Hrīṃ Hrīṃ), this three-syllabled mantra, O Goddess, bestows the fruit of all desires. (15)
And hear now another fruit of these very mantras, O beloved:
there is no restriction of time here, nor any defect caused by enemies, friends, and the like. (16)
There is no bodily affliction whatsoever, nor any exertion in its accomplishment;
whether by day or by night, recitation is auspicious everywhere. (17)
In this practice, there is certainly no contradiction between worldly enjoyment and liberation;
even a man attains liberation through enjoyment by means of this knowledge. 18.
Through the recitation and likewise through the meditation upon this [mantra], one shall obtain the fourfold liberation.
There is no knowledge equal to this; there is no recitation equal to this. (19)
There is no meditation equal to this, nor is there any austerity equal to this;
truly, truly, again truly, I speak with truth as my foundation. (20)
There is no knowledge equal to this, nor is there any accomplishment within its proper sphere.
Now, I shall briefly describe the unsurpassed ritual of worship. (21)
Who has the capacity for its full extent, or who knows it in its true essence?
Worship is said to be threefold: daily (nitya), occasional (naimittika), and optional (kāmya). || 22 ||
In that very context, I shall describe the daily worship; listen to it.
Bhairava is declared to be its seer (ṛṣi), and the Uṣṇik meter is proclaimed for it. || 23 ||
The ancient goddess Mahākālī has been proclaimed by the sages;
the application of this Vidyā, moreover, lies within the four aims of human life.
That which is performed by one devoid of the five purities is as if not performed at all; worship without the five purities leads to malevolent magic (*abhicāra*). (25)

Purification of the self, purification of the place, as well as the purification of the ritual substance, purification of the mantra, and purification of the deity—this is declared to be the fivefold purification. (26)
On a level and pure patch of ground, strewn with heaps of flowers,
one should first prepare a seat, such as a soft rug or a woolen blanket.
Having bowed again to the gurus on the left and to the omnipresent Gaṇapati on the right,
one should likewise perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) so that one becomes fit for worship.
Having performed *prāṇāyāma* and other preliminary rites according to the rules, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers and so forth.
First, one should say: "Obeisance to the Seer Śuddhibhairava. (29)
One should assign the Uṣṇik meter with a salutation to the mouth;
one's beloved Mahākālī is the deity, and one should offer salutation to her at the heart. (30)

First, "Hrīṃ, salutation to the seed-syllable," and then "Huṃ, salutation to the power"; having thus performed the ritual application (viniyoga) for the sake of poetic skill according to one's desire, one should perform the ritual placement (vinyāsa). || 31 ||
Having performed the placement of the *mātṛkā* alone, one should perform the placement of the seed-syllables (*bījanyāsa*).
Having placed "Oṃ Krāḥ" on the two thumbs, [one places] "Oṃ Krīḥ" on the two index fingers; "Namaḥ" [is placed on the middle fingers]. || 32 ||
Oṃ kra, having placed [it] on the two middle fingers; Oṃ krai, on the two ring fingers;
Oṃ krau, on the pair of little fingers; and likewise Oṃ kraḥ on the palms of the hands. || 33 ||

Furthermore, one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅgaka*) upon the heart and other parts using these [syllables] joined with their respective seed-syllables; one should place them in the form of the six long vowels, preceded by the *praṇava* (oṃ), together with their own seed-syllables. (34)
One should perform the deposition of the phonemes (varṇanyāsa) in such a way that one becomes identical with the Goddess:
one should deposit a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ in the heart. (35)
E, ai, o, au, aṃ, aḥ, ka, kha, ga, gha are on the right arm;
ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha, ña, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha are on the left arm. || 36 ||
One should place ṇa, ta, tha, da, dha, na, pa, pha, ba, and bha on the right shank;
and ma, ya, ra, la, va, śa, ṣa, sa, ha, la, and kṣa on the left shank. (37)
While reciting the root mantra either fivefold or sevenfold,
one should perform the supreme pervasive placement (vyāpaka-nyāsa) from the head down to the feet.
This is declared to be the "eternal placement" (nityanyāsa), which brings happiness to all.
Now I shall describe the meditation that bestows the form of Bhairava. (39)
In the city of Bhairava, situated in the midst of the Himalaya mountains,
in that divine place, the great sacred seat (mahāpīṭha), which is surpassed only by the pavilion of jewels.
There, one should meditate upon the primordial Mahākālī, whose lotus feet are served by the best of sages such as Nārada, and who is praised by Bhairava.
I bow to the auspicious Bhīmā, who has the hue of a blue lotus, whose full and lofty breasts form a pair,

who shines upon the throne of the sleeping Śrī-Hari, who possesses three eyes, who holds the mudrā and a sword in her hands, is endowed with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and is radiant in her variegated garments.
And I salute the Supreme Goddess, who wears a garland made of shimmering moonstones. 42.
I shall now proclaim the intermediate meditation; listen, O Gaurī, daughter of the Mountain!
There, upon that sacred seat, is the Great Goddess Kālī, who is served by the Dānavas. (43)

She has a body like a cloud, is naked, and is seated upon a corpse-head; she is the supreme goddess with three eyes, radiant with a pair of arrows hanging from her ears, and adorned with a garland of severed heads.
In her left lower and upper lotus-hands, she holds a human head and a sword, while in her right [hands]... [the rest of the verse follows].
Kālikā, whose mass of hair is liberated from fear of giving, should always be meditated upon. || 44 ||
Furthermore, I shall proclaim the meditation that is extremely difficult to attain:
[one should meditate upon] Kālī, whose face is formidable, who has terrible fangs, and who is three-eyed. (45)
One should remember her who is naked, wearing a girdle made of a row of arrows as rays, seated in the vīrāsana posture upon Mahākāla. (46)
Her cheeks were covered with the roots of the Vedas, she made a terrible sound,
was smeared with blood dripping from a garland of severed heads, and possessed full breasts.
She causes the entire earth to tremble with the clashing of her drums, which are intoxicated by wine;
she holds a sword in her left hand and a severed head in her right hand.

She is endowed with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, possesses a terrible face and a flickering tongue, and is adorned with ears decorated by arrows joined with the feathers of birds. || 49 ||
It was frequented by auspicious jackals of terrifying howls that had arisen at the time of universal dissolution,
and by Bhairavas known as Caṇḍa, who possessed fierce laughter, fierce cries, and fierce narrations.
Carrying human skeletons, they were intent on shouts of victory;
she was served by hosts of all the perfected ones (siddhas) and attended upon by sages.
Having performed any one of these meditations, the supreme practitioner should worship himself as the Self, saying "I am He," with mental offerings.
Then, having worshipped the Goddess, one should present two offerings of water (arghya);
one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) upon lotuses with fifteen or ten petals.
Having invoked the Great Goddess there with self-restraint and a concentrated mind,
he should then meditate upon the Great Goddess Kālikā, the ornament of the Kula.
One should worship Mahākāla with effort, and thereafter worship the power (śakti) of the sacred seat (pīṭha):
Kālī, Kapālinī, Kullā, Kurukullā, and Virodhinī.
Likewise, one should place Vipracittā outside in the hexagon;
furthermore, one should place Ugrā, Ugraprabhā, and Dīptā there in the triangle.
One should worship Mahākāla with effort, and then one should worship the Śaktis of the sacred seats (pīṭha):
Kālī, Kṛpālinī, Kullā, Kurukullā, and Virodhinī.
Likewise, one should place Vipracittā outside in the hexagon;
then, in the triangle there, one should place Ugrā, Ugreprabhā, and Dīptā.
One should place Nīlā, Ghanā, and Valākā in the outer triangle, and likewise Mātrā, Mudrā, and Nityā in the inner triangle. (59)

All of them were dark-complexioned, holding swords in their hands, adorned with garlands of severed heads, displaying the threatening gesture (tarjanī) with their left hands, and possessing pure smiles. || 60 ||
Having likewise invoked Brāhmī and the others, one should worship them in the order of the eastern petal and so forth:
Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, and likewise Maheśvarī. (61)
Cāmuṇḍā and Kaumārī likewise shine here;
Vārāhī and Nārasiṃhī are also to be worshipped in the same way. (62)
To all of them as well, an offering (bali) and likewise worship should be given;
as well as unguents, perfume, incense, lamps, and a drink.
The practitioners must perform worship three times for each [deity];
having worshipped them again with perfumes and other offerings, and having performed the recitation, they should offer the remainder.
One should honor the pledge (samaya) with the Goddess, together with the yoginīs and yogins;
[this includes] honey, meat, fish, and whatever constitutes the Kula practice.
Having given it to the Śakti, one should thereafter present it to the Guru;
having placed his permission upon one's head, one should then unite the remainder with oneself.
But he who performs the ancestral worship (kulapūjā) without honey and meat, his merit accumulated over a thousand lifetimes is destroyed. (67)
Therefore, with every effort, one should worship with the five *makāras*;
for there is no mantra without honey (*madhu*), nor is there honey without the mantra.
How can practitioners achieve success through mutual contradiction?
[For there is] the ritual employment of objects such as sacrificial pits, jars, and potsherds. (69)
It is contrary to the Saura Tantra, yet it yields great fruit in the Śaiva and Śākta traditions;
it is born from a fragment of the Cosmic Egg and is produced from every kind of jewel. (70)
White, yellow, fragrant, stainless, and of great brilliance;
or else, the supreme nectar flowing within this vessel. (71)
The internal dissolution is within the triangle in the middle;
outside of that is the mandala, vast as crystal and like the moon.
With that nectar, one should contemplate the supreme nectar outside of it;
[the stages are] the beginning, the youth, and the maturity, and at its end, the youth again.
Since the yogin, through these [offerings], becomes full of joy and himself consists of Śiva,
O Goddess of the gods, he should offer the general arghya (libation) in the final position.

Having offered the special arghya to Śiva, one becomes most beloved to the Goddess; having performed the ritual with its ancillaries and offered the general arghya to Śiva, one becomes established in his state.
Having spoken thus, that wise one who brings satisfaction to Śakti attains liberation through enjoyment; what is the use of much talk? (76)
The rule is to be understood as applying to men, never to women; by whatever means, in whatever way, at all times, and from whatever source [they may obtain it]. || 77 ||

Through the yoga of meditation upon women, there is no doubt that the remainder [of one's impurities] is purified—whether she be a girl, intoxicated with youth, an old woman, or likewise a young maiden. (78)
Or, having paid homage to one who is contemptible or greatly wicked, one should dismiss her;
likewise, striking them, censuring them, as well as crookedness and unpleasantness [should be avoided]. (79)
"In every way, it must not be done otherwise, for it would cause an obstruction to success.
Thus I have told you the remainder; O beloved, one should practice according to the characteristics."
Having understood the sequence of the daily worship with devotion, one shall attain perfection.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Mantra and Worship of Mahākālī," in the *Kaṅkālamālinī Tantra* of the Dakṣiṇāmnāya, consisting of one hundred and fifty thousand verses.
The Fifth Chapter.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O highly fortunate one, please describe the supreme *puraścaraṇa*.
And at what time should it be performed so that it bestows wonderful accomplishment in the Kali age? || 1 ||
The illustrious Lord said:
I shall explain the general procedure for *puraścaryā*; listen.
There is no inauspicious time; there is nothing inauspicious anywhere. (2)
There is no distinction between day and night, nor at twilight or the dead of night;
O Maheśānī, the concepts of "proper time" and "improper time" are nothing but delusion—of this there is no doubt. (3)
When the great dissolution has arrived, everything goes into Brahman;
at that most terrifying time, who experiences auspiciousness or inauspiciousness?
In this age of Kali, O Mahāmāyā, people become short-lived;
since the lifespan of all is unascertainable, how can there be concern for time, my dear?
O beloved, at whatever time one engages in meditation on Brahman, at that very time it becomes fruitful;
O Goddess, in the performance of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā), one should not concern oneself with the consideration of time.
In this [practice], there is no requirement for purity and the like, nor is there any defect such as prohibited actions;
here there is no restriction of direction or time, nor any restriction regarding posture and so forth.
O beautiful one, there is no restriction regarding time for recitation, nor even for worship and the like;
in the practice of this great mantra, the rule is conduct according to one's own will.
O fair-browed one, no unrighteousness exists when one acts with a joyful mind in Jambūdvīpa, in the region known as Bhārata, during the Kali age.
O Girijā, success will undoubtedly be attained from recitation even within six months;
that which has not been stated in any of the tantras, I shall tell you today. (10)
O fortunate one, O lady of beautiful limbs, O auspicious one with lotus-like eyes, listen to that by which perfection is attained in the Kali age within the land of Bhārata. (11)
I shall relate all of that today; listen with careful attention.
O lady of excellent hips, in the Kali age, mere recitation (japa) alone is praised.
Neither the lunar day, nor the vow, nor the fire-oblation, nor the ritual bath, nor the twilight worship is praised;
O Goddess, in the Kali age one cannot accomplish a mantra without the preliminary service (puraścaryā). 13.
O Goddess, the Satya and Tretā Yugas are characterized by the means for attaining happiness, while the Dvāpara is moderate;
but the Kali Age is always difficult to overcome and consists entirely of suffering.
Indeed, the essence of all tantras is said to reside within the Mahākālīs.
Having performed the morning rites and so forth, one should then perform the ritual bath. (15)
Having performed the twilight rites and libations in brief, O fair-faced one, as well as the worship according to the sequence of the respective chapters, O lady of excellent hips; (16)
Having placed [the deity] at the door of worship, one should offer the bali-oblation in the proper sequence;
likewise, one should perform three breath-restraints (prāṇāyāma) and offer a bali of black gram and rice.

O Goddess of the gods, having formed a mental resolve and performed worship, the practitioner of the offering of oblations (bali) should first know the single-syllable seed-mantra of Gaṇapati, which is "gaṃ". (18)
Then, having secretly drawn [the design] on the ground, the practitioner should offer an oblation (bali) resembling a ball (piṇḍa) with the mantra: "Oṃ Gaṃ, to Gaṇapati, svāhā. (19)
And in this manner, one should offer the *bali* everywhere upon the seed-syllable:
"Oṃ bhairavāya, then svāhā; then the *bali* to Bhairava. (20)
Oṃ kṣaṃ, svāhā to Kṣetrapāla; then the bali offering for Kṣetrapāla. Oṃ yāṃ, namaḥ svāhā to the Yoginīs; and the bali offering for the Yoginīs.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite, one should offer the bali-oblation in sequence as before;
O Goddess, one should avoid idle chatter here in the abode of the gods.
O auspicious lady, one should offer [the oblation] to Gaṇapati in the east, to Bhairava in the north,
to Kṣetrapāla in the west, and to the Yoginī in the south.
One should offer bali-oblations to Indra and the other deities for the sake of one's own welfare;
then one attains success, otherwise it results in nothing but ridicule. (24)
One pala of black gram paste, one pala of rice, half a tola of ghee, and half of a half-tola (one-quarter tola) of curd. || 25 ||
One should offer the bali-oblation with one *tolaka* of sugar for the sake of perfect accomplishment;
through the combination of these, O Śāmbhavī, the bali becomes effective. (26)
Then, O auspicious one, one should write the seed-syllable of Kūrma in the place of worship;
that seed-syllable consisting of the moon-bindu is called the Kūrma-bīja. (27)
One should establish the seat there and perform worship according to the sequence of the ritual manual;
then, having performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), one should thereafter perform breath control (prāṇāyāma).

He who performs the assignment of limbs (aṅganyāsa), the assignment of hands (karanyāsa), and the assignment of the Mātṛkās—indeed, he who performs the Mātṛkānyāsa is Śiva himself; there is no doubt about this. || 29 ||
Thereafter, one should wear the Rudrākṣa known as Bhīmatilaka;
O beloved, listen now to the greatness of the Rudrākṣa and of the sacred ash (bhasma).
The ash produced from cow dung and milk is said to be of the nature of fire;
one should purify it while reciting the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
O Goddess, [one should worship] in the region of the head, on the forehead, on the two shoulders, in the region of the eyebrows,
on the two arms, on both sides, in the region of the throat, and on the heart, O beloved.
O Maheśvarī, [one should worship] on the two ears, the back, the navel, and the mouth;
from the elbows to the ends of the arms, and on the armpits and necks, O Pārvatī. (33)
O Goddess, smear it on all the limbs; what more shall I tell you?
Then, with the middle finger, the ring finger, and the thumb, apply the *tilaka*.
The *tilaka* should consist of three lines, and these lines are considered to be of nine types:
Earth, Fire, Śakti, Kriyā-śakti, and Maheśvara; || 35 ||
O fortunate lady, the God has been proclaimed by you with devotion as the deity of the first line; however, O beautiful one, ashes are not the deity of the second line. (36)
If one should wear the Tripuṇḍra after constantly paying homage to these—the Supreme Self, the god Śiva, and the deity of the third [eye]—then [it is auspicious]. || 37 ||
Having performed this vow of Maheśvara, one becomes a master of supernatural powers (siddhi),
whether he be a celibate student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or likewise an ascetic.
One is liberated from the collection of great sins (mahāpātaka) and from all other transgressions, as well as from the sins of killing others such as kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and women. || 39 ||
O Subhageśvarī, one is liberated from the sins of killing a hero or a Brāhmaṇa;
even without mantras, he who performs [this rite] does so knowing its exalted majesty. (40)
One who bears the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) as a tilaka on the forehead is liberated from all sins, including the theft of another's property and the violation of another's wife. || 41 ||
Censuring others, seizing the fields of others, causing pain to others, speaking untruths, backbiting, harshness, and selling [images of] the gods. || 42 ||

Engaging in sexual union with menstruating girls or widows, and the selling of meat, hides, liquids, and the like, as well as salt; 45.
Such various and innumerable sins as these perish instantly by the wearing of the triple staff (tridaṇḍa). 46.
From the theft of Śiva’s property, from the disparagement of Śiva anywhere, and from the reviling of Śiva’s devotees, one is not purified even by penances. (47)
By wearing the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) upon the head, one becomes pure at that very moment,
even for the theft of the property of the gods or the theft of the property of a Brāhmaṇa.
O Great Goddess, O highly fortunate one, in this world families are always destroyed by fire and by the transgression against Brahmins. (49)
From this, as well as from the practice of wearing the triple mark (tripuṇḍra), there is protection for one's family;
he who has rudrākṣas upon his body and the triple mark upon his forehead [is thus protected]. (50)
Even if he were a Cāṇḍāla, he would be the most excellent among all castes; for whatever holy places exist in this world, and whatever rivers such as the Gaṅgā, [they are all present there]. || 51 ||
One who has the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) on the forehead is considered purified in every respect;

Ten million mantras of Śrī Viṣṇu and ten million mantras of Śiva—

He who applies the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) shall uplift a thousand ancestors and a thousand descendants born in his own lineage among mortals.
Endowed with the six qualities of sovereignty, having then attained a divine body,

And [he saw them] among the Vidyādharas, the Siddhas, the Gandharvas of great luster,
and the world-protectors such as Indra, each in their respective worlds in due order.
Having enjoyed vast pleasures in the cities of various regions,
one shall reach the station of Brahmā and dwell there for ten thousand kalpas.
He rejoices in the world of Viṣṇu for a lifespan of one hundred Brahmās,

He attains union with Śiva and is not born again—whether in the Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Saura, or Gāṇapatya [sects], O Pārvatī. (59)
O Maheśānī, the ash produced from the cow dung of that cow which exists in the form of Śakti is proclaimed to be the most excellent among them.
O lady of excellent hips, O woman of beautiful complexion, even for the Śaivas, the possession of the six qualities is auspicious;
indeed, ash is praised for liberation, youth, and life when applied to the Śakti.
For others, even for Śakti and the rest, the ash may be made from cow-dung;
this is the general rule, O fair-hipped one, my beloved—now hear the specific distinction.
O sinless one, the ash from cow-dung and firewood yields great fruit;
O Maheśvarī, the ash from the Viṣṇu-homa is ten million times more efficacious than the ash from the Homa.
O beautiful one, listen now to the rite of the Śiva-homa, which is twice that amount;
and O lady of sweet speech, the infinite rite of the oblation to one's own chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) performed with ashes.
I am not capable of describing its greatness even in hundreds of millions of kalpas;
what else shall I tell you regarding the path of yoga? 65.
O Goddess Mahākālī, O Śivā, in the Kali age, within the region of Jambūdvīpa known as Bhārata, the fire sacrifice (homa) is performed according to the sequence of one-tenth [of the recitation]. 66.
Those nihilists are in great delusion; one should perform only the fire-oblation (homa), either a hundred thousand, ten thousand, or a thousand times, O fair-faced one. (67)
Or one may perform one hundred and eight optional oblations (kāmyahoma);
and the daily oblation (nityahoma) should also be performed according to one's capacity, O Supreme Goddess.
In the daily worship, one should recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times, or one hundred and eight times, or fifty-eight times. (69)
According to the prescribed rule, one may perform thirty-eight, or twenty-eight, or eighteen,
or twelve, or ten, or eight [recitations].
And the fire sacrifice (homa), O Maheśānī, is likewise performed according to this prescribed number;
thus, O Deveśī, everywhere there is the great festival of the daily rites.
O Maheśānī, having thus smeared such ash upon his body, the practitioner [should also wear] a rosary made of human bone, which is worshipped as something marvelous.
O lady of excellent hips, O divine mistress, if one is capable, one should place it on the neck;
thereafter, O my beloved, listen to me regarding the wearing of a rosary of rudrākṣa beads.
Having done this, I remained with you in my father’s land.
O fortunate one, O lady of beautiful hips, listen to the Rudrākṣa, the supreme state. (74)
O Goddess, the Rudrākṣa causes the destruction of all sins, O Brahmāṇī;
whether one has fasted or eaten, and whether one is lowly or even lower than the lowly— (75)
Whoever wears a rudrākṣa is liberated from all sins;
the merit of wearing a rudrākṣa is equal to that of attaining absolute liberation (kaivalya). || 76 ||

O Śivā, he who wears a thousand of these meritorious great vows (mahāvrata), which are endowed with the power of thirty million sacred fords (tīrtha), of Rudrākṣa beads, [attains the highest state]. 77.
All the gods bow down to him; he is just like Rudra.
In the absence of the thousand-armed form, however, there are sixteen [arms] for each of the two sides.
One on the crest-lock, twelve on each of the two armors respectively, thirty-two in the region of the throat, and likewise forty on the head. (79)
He who wears six Rudrākṣas on each of his two ears and one hundred and eight on his heart is honored like Rudra himself.
He who wears Rudrākṣas combined with pearls, coral, crystal, sun-stones, moon-stones, and gold is Śiva himself. || 81 ||
O fair-faced one, even he who wears only rudrākṣas is not touched by sins, just as darkness does not touch the sun. (82)
A mantra recited with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads bestows infinite fruit;
yet for him on whose body there is not even a single rudrākṣa, O lady of excellent complexion, [the mantra is fruitless]. (83)
His birth would be as meaningless as one who bathes his head while wearing a rudrākṣa on his forehead without having applied the triple mark (tripuṇḍra). || 84 ||
The fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā arises for him; there is no doubt in this matter—for he who worships a rudrākṣa even without ablutions with water. (85)
One certainly obtains that very same fruit which results from the worship of Śiva, whether by means of [images] with one face, five faces, or likewise thirteen faces. (86)
By reciting it with fourteen faces, all accomplishments (siddhis) arise. O lady of excellent limbs, what is the use of much talk? Having performed this wondrous movement, [the goal is attained]. 87.
Having diligently worn the rudrākṣa, that practitioner becomes Śiva himself;
having first made a tilaka with sacred ash, one should thereafter wear the rudrākṣa. (88)
Then, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa), and performed worship,
the practitioner desiring success in the root mantra should perform the worship of the syllables (varṇapūjana).
Having smeared pure sandalwood upon the jar which embodies all colors, one should perform the worship of the thirty-six garlands of letters, which is distinguished by its breadth and height.
Having inscribed the letters of the alphabet, joined with all their constituent parts,
and having worshipped the Guru according to the prescribed rule, one should perform the ritual installation of the water-pot (ghaṭasthāpana).
One should worship the fifty letters of the Mātṛkā according to one's means;
having worshipped them with the five offerings and performed meditation with a clear mind, [one should proceed]. (92)
Resembling white lightning, with two arms and tremulous eyes,
she is clothed in black garments and wears a white upper cloth.
Richly adorned with various ornaments, radiant with a tilaka of vermilion, inflamed by the arrows of her sidelong glances, and with eyes slightly curved at the corners; (94)
One should meditate upon the eternal goddess, who bestows the perfection of mantras and whose nature is pure being;
she resembles red lightning, has two arms, and possesses tremulous eyes. (95)
Clad in white garments with a black cloth as an upper garment, richly adorned with various ornaments, and radiant with a tilaka mark of vermilion; 96.

One should meditate upon the eternal goddess, whose form is passion (rajas), who bestows the attainment of mantras, and whose eyes are curved and anointed with collyrium, blazing with the arrows of her sidelong glances. 97.
Resembling a wandering bee, she has two arms and tremulous eyes;
she is clothed in red garments with a black cloth as an upper garment. || 98 ||
Richly adorned with various ornaments, radiant with a tilaka of vermilion, inflamed by the arrows of her sidelong glances, and graced by the creeper-like play of her eyebrows. (99)
One should meditate upon the eternal goddess, who bestows the perfection of mantras and whose nature is darkness;
having meditated upon her and offered water for the feet and other honors, one should worship her, who consists of the three qualities, in due order.
"Oṃ, salutation to her whose form is the syllable *ūṃ*; one should worship her with water for the feet (*pādya*).
O fortunate one, through the initial meditation, one should worship the supreme [goddess] who consists of pure being (*sattvamayī*). (101)

Oṃ, salutation to her whose form is Kaṅkāra; one should worship with water for the feet and other offerings, while performing the second meditation on the seventeen-syllable mantra in its proper sequence. (102)

One should worship with water for the feet and other offerings to her whose form is the syllable *daṃ*, while performing the third meditation on the seventeen-syllable mantra in its proper sequence. (103)
In this manner, one should worship the fifty letters in sequence.
Thus, O auspicious lady, the worship of the fifty letters has been described to you. (104)
O auspicious lady, through the worship of the castes, the worship of the gods is accomplished;
through the worship of the castes, there shall be the worship of the eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇiman*. (105)
There are seventy million great vidyās and likewise secondary vidyās;
there are also ten million mantras of Śrī Viṣṇu and ten million mantras of Śiva.
Through worship, everything is worshipped, and it bestows success upon all classes;
having first uttered the *praṇava*, one should recite [the mantra] a thousand times at the mouth of the *kuṇḍalinī*.
Then, O auspicious one, one should recite the root-vidyā two thousand times;
thereafter, O fortunate mother, one should recite the supreme Dīpinī.
First, having uttered the Gāyatrī, then the root mantra, and then the Praṇava, O Bhīme, through the conjunction with the word "bhayānām" (of fears). || 109 ||
O Great Goddess, one should always recite this celebrated Dīpinī mantra,
and indeed recite it a thousand times at the mouth of the Kuṇḍalinī.
One should recite the supreme *Dīpinī* Vidyā at the beginning of the *Praṇava* within the *Gāyatrī*.
Listen, O beloved, as I shall declare the *Gāyatrī*: *a ṅa ma ma ṅa na*. (111)
This six-syllabled mantra is declared to be the Gāyatrī;
O woman of excellent complexion, one obtains its fruit at that very moment.
One should perform recollection within the center of Kuṇḍalinī by means of the mind together with Unmanī,
[visualizing her] situated in the middle of the lunar orb upon the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus.
Free from all conceptual constructions, the seventeenth digit becomes known as Unmanī; for she indeed severs the bonds of worldly existence.
The yogi who is accompanied by Unmanī is a true yogi; without Unmanī, he is not a yogi.
One should contemplate the intellect joined with the goad and endowed with the flower of Unmanī. (115)
One should remember Unmanī, who bestows perfection through the recollection of the color of the mind;
one should remember the nectar of a red luster arising from the union with Kuṇḍalī.
That indeed is to be known as the flower of Unmanī, which is most difficult to attain. (116)
Having taken by the hand that *Kuṇḍalinī*— the *Haṃsa* who is eternally possessed of infinite and immeasurable qualities, and the Power (*Śakti*) who has emerged from her own support,
the mother of all beings— the beloved one, radiant as ten million suns and overflowing with the nectar of the Name, [returned] to her own abode.
One of steady mind should meditate upon that Goddess, the deluder of the world, by means of her coming and going. || 117 ||
Thus has been described to you that meditation which conquers death and is free from ailment;
without the Manonmanī mantra, and without meditation, recitation is in vain.
Then, having made the formal resolve and meditated for the sake of attaining mastery over the root mantra,

O auspicious lady, whatever offering of bali is given day after day to Gaṇapati and the other deities, that very bali is always considered equivalent to sacrificial oblation (haviṣya).
Then, having fully worshipped the remaining deity as desired, he should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya) together with his wife;

If his wife, being beautiful and self-restrained, should recite [the mantra], then the practitioner, united with Śakti, attains the fruit. || 125 ||
If one is devoid of power, there will be suffering; what is the use of ten million rounds of *puraścaraṇa*?
The male practitioner should subsist on sacrificial food (*haviṣya*), while the female practitioner should be free from that restriction.
She ate as she desired, her mouth filled with betel-leaf,
enriched by various ornaments and attire, and delighted by the fragrance of incense.
"One should avoid from afar a woman who is devoid of Śiva.
The Goddess said: "O Lord, at the time of reciting the Gāyatrī, what should she who is qualified recite? (128)
Śrī Śiva said:
If one who is qualified should mutter the Gāyatrī-majapā-vidyā... [verses 29 and 30a are missing].
Having meditated according to the previously mentioned procedure and having performed the worship, || 131 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should perform mental recitation with the mind fixed upon that;

Having formed a resolve with devotion according to the prescribed rule for the sake of attaining mastery over the root mantra,

One should recite the mantra ten times, which purifies the tongue;
thereafter, remaining silent, one should continue reciting the mantra until midday.
To his left is his consort; the practitioner should mutter her single-syllable mantra.
The practitioner is the very form of Śiva, and the practitioner’s consort is the very form of Śivā. || 138 ||
Through mutual contemplation alone, divinity is certainly born;
the wise one should recite the mantra while placing the *praṇava* at the beginning and at the end. (139)
Having recited the mantra ten times or seventeen times, he should then perform the recitation;
beginning at the time of dawn, he should continue the recitation until midday.
In this manner, one should perform [the practice] every day until the hundred thousand [recitations] are completed;
after the second watch of the day, one should perform the daily worship and other rites.
Then, having performed his ablutions, the wise one partook of sacrificial food (haviṣya);
his wife, who was the embodiment of power and devoted to her husband, did likewise.
If she should desire those with whom she would enjoy herself, adorned for the banquet,
one should mutter the mantra on the bed at night during the period of ten *daṇḍas*.
With his mouth filled with betel and gladdened by the fragrance of incense,
and with the Śrī-Śakti on his left, he should mutter the syllables of the practitioner.
The practitioner, having attained success, should recite the mantra during the day;
if he recites it every day, having performed the concealment of the beginning and the end [of the mantra], [he shall succeed]. 145.
Then one attains success; otherwise, from its manifestation, there is only loss.
Having encased [the mantra] with the Mātṛkā and endowed it with the lunar bindu, [one attains success]. || 146 ||
One should recite the mantra every day in both forward and reverse order;
O fortunate and mature woman, one should recite the mantra every day at the beginning of the recitation.
Therefore, O blessed one, the preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) has been described;
when the puraścaraṇa is completed, one should worship the divine Guru.
Then the mantra becomes perfected through the worship of the Guru and the Deity, even in the land of Jambūdvīpa, in the region of Bhārata, and during the Kali age. 149.
O auspicious one, one should avoid the ten-fold portion; there is never a fire-oblation (homa) [in that case].
O Goddess, in the Kali age, the ten-fold portion is performed according to the five-limbed rite in its proper sequence.

O Maheśānī, the practitioner of mantra should not perform the rite of *puraścaryā* anywhere except in an auspicious place; if, through delusion, the best of practitioners should nevertheless perform it, [the following occurs]. 151.
O sinless one, the loss of accomplishment and great misfortune arise in Bhārata;
however, through the worship of the Guru and the Deity, it becomes fully restored tenfold. (152)
Therefore, O Great Goddess, one should worship the feet of the Guru with devotion;
one should give a sacrificial fee to the Guru consisting of gold accompanied by a garment. (153)
One should likewise give grain, sesame seeds, or even a milch cow;
otherwise, everything is fruitless—what is the use of performing ten million recitations? (154)
The meal for a maiden is peaceful and bestows all accomplishments;
by him who has fed a maiden, the three worlds have been fed. (155)
O beloved, through worshiping her, beholding her, delighting in her, and touching her, everything becomes fully accomplished for the practitioner whose mind is devoted. (156)
Having completed the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa), one should perform the heroic practice (vīrasādhana);
by the mere performance of which even one of dull fortune attains success. || 157 ||
Free from attachment and delusion regarding children, wife, and wealth, I shall either accomplish the mantra or cast off this body. || 158 ||
Having thus undertaken the vow and diligently propitiated the Guru, and having performed everything including the offering of oblations (bali) and all mental worship; || 159 ||
The great annual worship is performed during the autumn season;
during that fortnight, one should especially perform the preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa).

One should perform the rites of fire-offerings, worship, and so forth according to one's capacity;
especially on the seventh lunar day and other such occasions, one should worship one's chosen deity.
One should be intent on fasting from the eighth day until the ninth;
on the night of the eighth and ninth days, one should perform worship and a great festival.
In this manner, the practitioner with a steady mind should perform the recitation and other rites;
O lady of excellent hips, he should perform the worship of the maiden along with Śakti. 164.

Having thus performed the preliminary rite, the practitioner shall attain the state of Śiva.

during the autumn season, at the great festival of the Great Goddess upon her awakening. (166)

likewise with all ritual offerings, garments, ornaments, and decorations.
By means of buffaloes, goats, and rams, a man shall obtain the fourfold aims of life;
by this very procedure, he should offer an animal at the junction of time on the eighth lunar day.

Having performed the preliminary rite (*puraścaryā*) in this manner, what is there that the practitioner cannot accomplish?

At the junction of time on the eighth lunar day, having entered the house of one hundred and eight creepers according to the ritual rules, the practitioner of mantra should diligently worship them.

One becomes a great adept instantly by seeing and worshipping the creeper.

Exceeding the number eight, they belong to the category of those numbered nine and so forth; endowed with qualities such as youth and the like, they are superior and arrogant in their desires. (177)
For that house where women reside is indeed a bower of creepers;
or else, the *puraścaraṇa* is described in another manner.
O Great Goddess, the practitioner should perform the previously mentioned rites during the seasons beginning with Hemanta;
having attained perfection, he shall become a lord of all enjoyments. (179)
