At that time, the practitioners shall become accomplished; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
However, if there is a delay in attaining accomplishment, I shall explain the means for it here. (210)
O Dear One, [the rites of] causing wandering, awakening, subjugation, and likewise crushing, as well as nourishing, satisfying, and thereafter burning; 211.
These seven expedients exist, having been established during the Tretā Yugas;
likewise, O auspicious lady, they exist in the Dvāpara age, and the seventh expedient is remembered [to persist] as well.

O auspicious lady, in the Kali age, it is not recommended to perform the mantra-repetition of the one spoken by the seven Śaṅkaras, which involves the practice of ḍākinīs and the like; rather, one should repeat the mantra one hundred thousand times.
If success is not achieved by encircling [the mantra] with the *ḍākinī*,
one should encircle it with the *rākiṇī* and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
If success is not achieved after encircling [the mantra] with Rākiṇī,
one should encircle it with Lākinī and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
If success does not arise after encasing [the mantra] with Lākinī,
one should encase it with Kākinī and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
If success does not arise after encasing [the mantra] with the *kākinī*,
one should encase it with the *śākinī* and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Having encircled it with the Śākinī, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times with a concentrated mind;
then the mantra will become perfected—there is no need for further deliberation on this point.
If success does not arise after having performed the encapsulation with Lākinī,
one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, encapsulated by Sattvarūpiṇī.
If success does not arise when [the mantra] is encapsulated by Sattvarūpiṇī,
then one should employ the Mātṛkā in the form of phonemes, beginning with the letter *ka* and ending with the letter *kṣa*.
Having performed the *saṃpuṭita* (encasement) in that manner, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
for mantras such as those with broken syllables (*chinnavidyā*) have been described in various tantras. (221)
These attain accomplishment through the state of the letters of the Mātṛkā;
mantra-accomplishment will certainly occur—there is no need for deliberation on this point. (222)
If success is not achieved by wrapping [the mantra] with the syllables (varṇa),
then one should wrap it with the Guru-mantra and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
"By the grace of the Guru and the God, one shall attain incomparable perfection.
Śrī Pārvatī said: "O Ādideva, O Mahādeva, tell me the concealment of the beginning and the end."
O Lord, if it is not told to me, then I shall abandon this body.
The venerable Īśvara said:
How can I describe that subtle concealment of the beginning and the end?
In the Kali age, among the regions of Jambūdvīpa, people are remembered as the lowest of beings.
In every household, people will be devoid of devotion to the guru;
all will be intent on wicked deeds and bereft of supreme knowledge.
All will become practitioners of worldly conduct in every household;
without a thorough knowledge of the [sacred] sounds, a twice-born man may become a giver of mantras.
O Goddess of the gods, that Śrīmatī-mantra of mine is said to be the mantra that grants success everywhere, [liberating one] from the bonds arising from worldly existence.
Therefore, O beloved of my life, a doubt arises in me as to how [this could be]. || 228 ||
The illustrious Bhairavī said: O Lord of Beings, O highly fortunate one, show mercy upon my heart!
Let it be told, let it be told, O God, for we are your servants. (229)
The illustrious Lord said:
"O blessed mother, listen; out of compassion I shall tell you.
First is the seed-syllable of Ḍākinī, which consists of sixteen syllables for a young woman. (230)
A Ā I Ī U Ū Ṛ Ṝ Ḷ Ḹ E AI O AU A AḤ—this is declared to be the supreme seed-syllable (bīja) of the God of Gods.
If one recites the mantra a hundred thousand times, having encased it between the first and last [syllables], [the goal is attained]. 231.
Then, O lady of excellent hips, one is perfected; my word is not otherwise.
Now I shall fully explain the wonderful seed-syllable of the Ḍākinīs.
By merely reciting it once, [the merit] would be as that of the Satya and Tretā Yugas. || 233 ||
Ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha, ña—these ten, O Maheśvarī, are the wonderful seed-syllables of the Rākinīs, which I have declared to you out of devotion. (234)
Ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa, ta, tha, da, dha, na—this is the group of ten, O Supreme Goddess.
Thus, out of devotion, I have explained to you the determination of the seed-syllables (bīja) of the Lākinīs. (235)
Now I shall fully proclaim Kākinī, the bestower of accomplishment, O Goddess worshipped by heroes! She consists of the syllables pa, pha, ba, bha, ma, ya, ra, la, and ā. (236)
The seed-syllable of Kākinī, which bestows the fruits of the four aims of life, has been explained.
Now, O fortunate one, listen as I shall fully describe Śākinī. (237)
Va, śa, ṣa, and sa—O Dear One, this four-syllabled seed-mantra bestows desired objects;
it is the seed of the Śākinīs, which grants the four aims of human life. || 238 ||
Now I shall fully explain, O fortunate one, listen to Hākinī;
the seed-syllable of Hākinī—HAḤ LAḤ KṢAḤ—is the swift bestower of spiritual accomplishments. || 239 ||
Listen to the seed-syllable (bīja) whose nature is that of the *sattva*, which bestows accomplishment:
a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ, e, ai, o, au, aṃ, aḥ. || 240 ||
The great seed-syllable of sixteen letters is proclaimed to be situated in the midst of the *sattva*; this seed-syllable, whose nature is *rajas*, bestows swift accomplishment. (241)
Ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha, ña, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa, ta, tha—this group of seventeen syllables is indeed proclaimed to be in the midst of the *rajas*. 242.
I shall now tell you of that beautiful seed-syllable composed of darkness:
da, dha, na, pa, pha, ba, bha, ma, ya, ra, la, va, śa, ṣa, sa, ha, kṣa. || 243 ||
This seventeen-syllable [mantra] has indeed been proclaimed as being in the midst of Tamas;
now I shall fully describe the wonderful seed-syllable of the Mātṛkās.
a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ e ai o au aḥ aḥ ka kha ga gha ṅa ca cha ja jha ña ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa ta tha da dha na pa pha ba bha ma ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha kṣa.
This indeed is proclaimed as the fifty-syllabled Mātṛkā;
one should perform the recitation by enclosing it in forward and reverse order.
O Great Goddess, up to one hundred thousand recitations, one becomes a perfected being (siddha) without a doubt;
the seed-syllable of the Guru is taught as the two syllables "gu-ru."
Then there are the goddesses known as Ḍākinī, Rākinī, Lākinī, Kākinī, Śākinī, and Hāhinī; thereafter follows Sattvarūpā. || 247 ||
O Supreme Goddess, the Guru is of the nature of Rajas, of the nature of Tamas, and has the form of Mātṛkā;
these indeed constitute the fifty-syllable form.
The Ḍākinī is the Great Goddess who bestows the siddhi of aṇimā;
Rākiṇī bestows the siddhi of laghimā, and likewise Lākinī. (249)
Kākinī bestows the attainment of siddhi and grants all that is desired;
Śākinī bestows the siddhi of greatness, and after her is Hākinī.
She bestows the accomplishment of mastery over desires through mere recitation;
she is likewise of the nature of purity (sattva), of the nature of darkness (tamas), and of the nature of passion (rajas). (251)
O Great Goddess, these indeed bestow the fourfold aims of human life;
she who takes the form of the fifty letters bestows nirvāṇa itself.
"The Guru bestows the entire, imperishable knowledge of the universe.
Thus, out of devotion, I have related to you this definitive teaching concerning the Ḍākinīs and others. (253)
Ḍākinī, Rākiṇī, Lākinī, Kākinī, Śākinī, and Lākinī—O Goddess, these are the deities of the letters here. (254)
These six are the presiding deities of the qualities and the perfected letters;
without the knowledge of the Ḍākinīs and others, [the realization] is distinct for each individual letter. (255)

If one recites the mantra out of ignorance, or consumes the [substances] of the ḍākinīs and others without a thorough knowledge of the phonemes, what is the use of ten million rounds of purificatory rites? (256)
For him, everything will be suffering, like weeping in the forest.
Listen, O lady of pure smiles, I shall explain the meditation of the ḍākinīs. (257)
The meditations are as follows:
[one should visualize her] resembling the autumn moon, with two arms and tremulous eyes, radiant with a vermilion tilaka, and her eyes adorned with collyrium. (258)

For the sake of attaining mastery over the mantra of Ḍākinī, one should meditate upon the eternal one who has a moon-like face, is clothed in black garments, and is adorned with various ornaments. 259.
Resembling the rising sun, she has two arms and deer-like eyes;
she is radiant with a vermilion tilaka and her eyes are adorned with collyrium.
For the sake of attaining mastery over the mantra of Rākinī, one should meditate upon the eternal Śaśimukhī, who is clothed in white garments and adorned with various ornaments.
Resembling the color of vermilion, possessing two arms and eyes like those of a wagtail, she is illuminated by a tilaka of vermilion, with her eyes adorned with collyrium. || 262 ||
For the sake of attaining mastery over the mantra of Lākinī, one should meditate upon the eternal goddess who wears white garments, is adorned with various ornaments, and has a face like the moon.
Resembling barley-alkali in complexion, she has two arms and lotus-like eyes;
she is radiant with a vermilion tilaka and her eyes are adorned with collyrium.

For the sake of attaining mastery over the Kākinī mantra, one should meditate upon the eternal Kākinī, who is clothed in white garments, adorned with various ornaments, and possesses a moon-like face. 265.
Resembling white light, with two arms and deer-like eyes, she is radiant with a vermilion tilaka and her eyes are adorned with collyrium. || 266 ||

For the sake of attaining mastery over the Śākinī mantra, one should meditate upon the eternal Śākinī, who has a moon-like face, is clothed in black garments, and is adorned with various ornaments. || 267 ||
She has a luster that is white, black, and reddish; she has two arms and tremulous eyes;
she resembles a hovering bee, and her locks of hair are curled and long.
She was radiant with a tilaka mark of vermilion, her eyes were anointed with collyrium,
she wore garments of red cloth, and a white cloth as an upper garment.
One should constantly meditate upon the moon-faced Hākinī for the sake of attaining perfection in her mantra. || 269 ||
O Goddess of gods, the meditation on the one consisting of the three qualities has been previously described;
now I shall fully explain the supreme meditation on the Mātṛkā.
[One should meditate upon her] whose face, arms, palms, waist, and chest are adorned with the fifty letters of the alphabet;
who wears a radiant crescent moon bound upon her crown; whose breasts are full and high;
and who holds in her lotus-like hands a mudrā, a rosary, a jar brimming with nectar, and a book.
I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who possesses three eyes and bears a pure radiance. || 271 ||
O Maheśānī, even for the Guru, one should perform the previously mentioned meditation.
O lady of excellent hips, having worshipped with water for the feet and other offerings, one should mutter the mantra;
for whichever deity there is, whatever seed-syllable and whatever mantra has been previously mentioned, that is the determination for that [deity]. (272)
Aṃ, obeisance to Ḍākinī, svāhā; kaṃ, obeisance to Kākinī, and then:
ṭaṃ, obeisance to Lākinī, svāhā; paṃ, obeisance to Kākinī, and then. || 273 ||
"Vaṃ, obeisance to Śākinī, svāhā; haṃ, obeisance to Hākinī"—having spoken thus, one should worship them with the respective meditations and ritual offerings. || 274 ||
If one recites the mantra after encasing it with the previously mentioned seed-syllable, then the mantra—even if corrupted by defects such as curses—will become effective. (275)
Thus has been told to you this divine [teaching], which is approved for the Kali age;
it exists in Bhāratavarṣa during the Kali age, and never in any other land. (276)
The sixteen treasuries beginning with Śamā, conjoined with the siddhis of the Ḍākinīs; and the ten treasuries beginning with Caṇḍikā, conjoined with the siddhis of the Kākinīs. || 277 ||

The determination of the siddhi of Lākinī is the treasury of the ten [mantras] beginning with Śama; the determination of the siddhi of Kākinī is the treasury of the ten [mantras] beginning with Gada. || 278 ||

The determination of the accomplishment of the Śākinīs begins with "Kalyāṇī" and so forth, and ends with "vilakṣaṇā"; the determination of the accomplishment of the Hākinīs begins with "baddhā" and so forth, and ends with "vilakṣaṇā. || 279 ||
O blessed lady, without the Guru-deva, effort is entirely fruitless;
O beautiful one, in this Kali age, there is only strife between teacher and disciple. (280)
There will be no doubt regarding the blow between the teacher and the disciple;
thus everything concerning Kālikā, which is very difficult to obtain, has been told to you. (281)
In the Kali age, Lord Bhairava, Kālikā, Tārā the Great Vidyā, and likewise Tripurasundarī are ever awake. (282)
O Dear One, [the goddesses] are Dhanadā, Chinnamastā, Mātaṅgī, Bagalāmukhī, Tvaritā, Annapūrṇā, and likewise Vāgvādinī. (283)
Mahiṣaghnī, Viśālākṣī, Tāriṇī, Bhuvaneśikā, Dhūmāvatī, Bhairavī, and likewise Pratyaṅgirā and the others. || 284 ||
Durgā and Śākambharī are indeed asleep during the Kali age;
by the recitation of their mantra, their sleep is broken. (285)
O Goddess, when their sleep is interrupted, a loss of spiritual power (siddhi) occurs;
how much more so would there be a loss in their recitation and worship as they progress further? || 286 ||
Knowledge is praised among Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras; and truthfulness and the like are [praised] in all four ages and among all castes at all times. (287)
The Kālikā-vidyā is highly praised, and I shall explain the means for its realization so that its fruit may be understood and accomplishment may arise. (288)
If one recites the ḍākinī mantra a thousand times at night, then success will arise after a long time; there is no doubt about this. || 289 ||
O auspicious one, honored by heroes, women and Śūdras never have the requirement of *puraścaryā*; for them, recitation (*japa*) and worship (*pūjā*) are always recommended. (290)
O auspicious Mother, during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, the highest accomplishment arises for Śūdras, provided they possess devotion to the Guru. (291)
Then one attains accomplishment, especially through devotion to the Guru.
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Śrī Kaṅkālamālinī Tantra of the Dakṣiṇāmnāya.
And the book is completed.
